title: Review: The Player Report
explanation: Level 3 review! Remember the players table from Lesson 6? Imagine your boss wants a report on the players: how many there are, how much they play, and where they're from. Use everything from Level 3: COUNT, SUM, AVG, GROUP BY, and HAVING. Some tasks also mix in older skills like CASE WHEN and dates.

lines.explain: Show each country, plus the most hours any player there has played.

tasks.prompt: Show the total number of players (call it total_players) and the total hours they've played together (call it total_hours).
tasks.answer: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_players, SUM(hours_played) AS total_hours FROM players;
hints: Two aggregate functions in one SELECT: one to count, one to add up.
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_players, SUM(hours_played) AS total_hours

tasks.prompt: Label players 'Casual' (under 100 hours), 'Regular' (under 300 hours), or 'Hardcore' (everyone else) in a column called player_type. Then count how many are in each type (call it num_players).
tasks.answer: SELECT CASE WHEN hours_played < 100 THEN 'Casual' WHEN hours_played < 300 THEN 'Regular' ELSE 'Hardcore' END AS player_type, COUNT(*) AS num_players FROM players GROUP BY player_type;
hints: Build the label with CASE WHEN, then GROUP BY the label, just like Lesson 10.
SELECT CASE WHEN hours_played < 100 THEN 'Casual' WHEN hours_played < 300 THEN 'Regular' ELSE 'Hardcore' END AS player_type, COUNT(*) AS num_players ... GROUP BY player_type

solution_lines.explain: Everyone else is Hardcore. Name the label player_type.
Count the players in each group.

tasks.prompt: Show each country with more than 1 player, and the total hours played there (call it total_hours).
tasks.answer: SELECT country, SUM(hours_played) AS total_hours FROM players GROUP BY country HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
hints: Group by country. The 'more than 1 player' part is about groups, so it goes in HAVING.

solution_lines.explain: Show each country and its total hours.
Only keep countries with more than 1 player. You can filter on a count even if it's not in the SELECT.

tasks.prompt: Show how many players signed up each year. Call the year signup_year and the count new_players, oldest year first.
tasks.answer: SELECT strftime('%Y', signup_date) AS signup_year, COUNT(*) AS new_players FROM players GROUP BY signup_year ORDER BY signup_year ASC;
hints: Pull the year out with strftime() from Lesson 6, then group by it.
SELECT strftime('%Y', signup_date) AS signup_year, COUNT(*) AS new_players ... GROUP BY signup_year ORDER BY signup_year ASC

solution_lines.explain: Pull the year out of each sign-up date.
Count the players in each year.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: how many rows will this return?
tasks.code:
SELECT country
FROM players
GROUP BY country
HAVING AVG(hours_played) > 200;
hints: Work out the AVERAGE hours for each country, not the single biggest player.
USA averages 477 and the UK averages 275. The Philippines is close, at 198, but that's not over 200.

solution_lines.explain: Keep countries whose average is over 200: just the USA (477) and the UK (275). The Philippines just misses at 198.

recap: Level 3 complete! You can now summarise data, group it, and filter groups. That's the core of real data analysis.
